# NeRF Editing and Inpainting Procedures

Also called: NeRF Editing, NeRF Inpainting, 3D Content Editing

## Overview
NeRF Editing and Inpainting Procedures modify a pre-trained [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) to remove, add, or alter objects and textures while maintaining multi-view consistency. They solve the problem of 3D editing consistency, which is difficult because [standard NeRFs](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) entangle geometry and appearance, and 2D editing tools lack 3D coherence. These methods are distinguished from standard training by their focus on modifying an existing representation rather than learning it from scratch, often leveraging 2D priors (diffusion, inpainting) or semantic features to guide the optimization or rendering of the radiance field.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a radiance field representation $f_\theta$ that maps 3D coordinates $\mathbf{x}$ and viewing directions $\mathbf{d}$ to density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$. The core mechanism involves either optimizing the network parameters $\Theta$ to fit new constraints or modifying the output values $(\sigma, \mathbf{c})$ on-the-fly during rendering.

The [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md) remains the fundamental output mechanism for all methods:
$$ \hat{C}(r) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i c_i $$
where $w_i = T_i (1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i))$, $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$, and $\delta_i = t_i - t_{i-1}$ [S1, 12491-nerf-editing-procedure.md].

Common strategies include:
1.  **Optimization-based:** Minimizing a loss function that combines photometric reconstruction with guidance from 2D priors (e.g., inpainted images, depth maps, or semantic features) [12372-nerf-in-inpainting-optimization.md, 12405-adaptive-view-selection-for-inpainting.md].
2.  **Feature Distillation:** Training a dedicated [feature field](#12995-feature-fields.md) to disentangle semantic information from appearance, enabling editing via semantic masks without retraining the geometry [12068-dff-decomposing-nerf-for-editing-via-feature-field-distillat.md].
3.  **On-the-fly Modification:** Altering $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{c}$ during [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) based on semantic probabilities or geometric masks, bypassing weight updates [12491-nerf-editing-procedure.md].
4.  **Generative Priors:** Using [diffusion models](#10443-diffusion-models-ddpms.md) to generate pseudo-observations or inpainted reference views that guide the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) optimization to fill missing or unwanted regions [8658-progressive-inpainting-and-erasing.md, 11860-deceptive-nerf-3dgs-pipeline.md, 13952-reference-guided-controllable-inpainting-of-nerfs.md].

## Subtopics

### [Progressive Inpainting-and-Erasing](8658-progressive-inpainting-and-erasing.md)
A method for reconstructing a panoramic NeRF from a single input panorama by iteratively expanding the field of view. It solves geometry conflicts arising from inpainting invisible regions by erasing conflicting geometry from supervision. Choose this when starting from a single panorama and needing to expand the view consistently.

### [Deceptive-NeRF/3DGS Pipeline](11860-deceptive-nerf-3dgs-pipeline.md)
A sparse-view reconstruction method that enhances NeRF or 3DGS by generating synthetic pseudo-observations via a diffusion model during training. It distinguishes itself by enforcing 3D view consistency through an uncertainty map derived from epipolar reprojection. Choose this for sparse-view reconstruction where geometric plausibility is critical.

### [DFF (Decomposing NeRF for Editing Via Feature Field Distillation)](12068-dff-decomposing-nerf-for-editing-via-feature-field-distillat.md)
Enables 3D semantic segmentation and editable novel-view synthesis by distilling semantic features from a pre-trained 2D teacher network (LSeg/[DINO](#6425-dino-vit-feature-extraction.md)) into a neural radiance field. It sets itself apart by creating a dedicated feature field for semantic-aware [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md), avoiding the view-inconsistency of image-based inpainting. Choose this for semantic editing (deletion, extraction) requiring multi-view consistency.

### [Blended-NeRF](12273-blended-nerf.md)
A framework for editing specific regions of interest (ROI) in an existing NeRF based on text prompts and a user-defined 3D ROI box. It solves local 3D editing by training a generator NeRF and blending it with the original scene using volumetric blending. Choose this for text-guided object insertion or replacement within a defined 3D volume without semantic decomposition.

### [NeRF-In Inpainting Optimization](12372-nerf-in-inpainting-optimization.md)
A framework for removing unwanted objects from a pre-trained NeRF by optimizing model parameters using color and depth guidance from 2D images. It enables free-form inpainting without category-specific training. Choose this for object removal where 2D inpainting and depth completion priors are available.

### [Adaptive View Selection for Inpainting](12405-adaptive-view-selection-for-inpainting.md)
A method for 3D scene de-occlusion and inpainting that combines a pretrained 2D image inpainter with multi-view NeRF optimization. It solves inconsistent texture synthesis by dynamically selecting between 2D priors and multi-view geometric consistency based on local texture richness. Choose this for inpainting occluded regions where texture detail varies.

### [NeRF Editing Procedure](12491-nerf-editing-procedure.md)
Modifies a radiance field by altering density and color values on-the-fly during volume rendering based on semantic probabilities or geometric masks. It solves consistent 3D editing (deletion, colorization, translation) without changing stored network weights. Choose this for fast, inference-time editing using semantic guidance.

### [Reference-guided Controllable Inpainting of NeRFs](13952-reference-guided-controllable-inpainting-of-nerfs.md)
Performs 3D inpainting using a single inpainted reference view to guide geometry and appearance, ensuring view consistency and generating view-dependent effects (VDEs). It distinguishes itself by avoiding view inconsistencies at distances far from the reference and handling disocclusions. Choose this when a single high-quality inpainted reference view is available.

### Semantic Inpainting for Neural Fields
A 3D content editing capability allowing editing of neural fields through simple interfaces like free-form sketching or language instructions [S1]. Given a user-supplied edit in a single reference view, the encoding of a neural field automatically propagates this edit to all views [S1]. This propagation promotes consistency between all views thanks to the implicit geometrical and photometric priors embodied by the neural network, preserving the structure of the whole scene [S1]. Described in reference [19] [S1].

### Post-Refinement Strategy
A strategy employed after the NeRF has been trained on updated data to enhance consistency by generating a more accurate target for each view using the modified Instruct-Pix2Pix with averaging architecture [S2]. It uses the rendered image as input while continuing to use the mixup image as a condition [S2].

## Background
Neural rendering has evolved from explicit physical modeling to data-driven inference, enabling high photorealism and real-time rates [S1]. The concept of "distilling" 2D generative knowledge (e.g., from Imagen or Stable Diffusion) to 3D geometry without 3D supervision has become a key trend, exemplified by [DreamFusion](#12087-dreamfusion.md) [S1]. Recent developments allow editing neural fields with ease through simple interfaces, such as semantic inpainting where edits in a single view propagate to all views [S1]. Methods like ViCA-NeRF employ post-refinement strategies using modified Instruct-Pix2Pix to enhance consistency [S2]. The field continues to accelerate with breakthroughs in [Instant-NGP](#6604-instant-ngp.md), 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md), and synergies with generative approaches [S1].
